title: authorization gap observed during dedicated rolling upgrade due to alias propagation ordering
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
During a rolling control-plane upgrade on Dedicated clusters we observed a transient authorization failure for a small fraction of production requests. The client received 403s for otherwise-valid API key usages when requests were routed to nodes that had received cache updates in a different order than the control-plane alias swap.

What happened (root cause hypothesis):
- We rotate API key aliases in the control plane using a two-step: write new alias mapping then invalidate edge caches via an async fan-out job.
- Under load + rolling upgrade ordering differences, some edge nodes received the cache invalidation before the authoritative alias mapping write was visible (eventual ordering across regions).
- That created a short window where the edge cache mapped an api_key -> old_org or missing binding, but the control plane had already rejected tokens tied to the new alias, causing 403s for valid requests.
- The scope of affected customers: Hosted small, Dedicated customers on multi-node pools, and Private deployments with eventual cache invalidation configured. We saw the largest customer impact on two Dedicated tenants doing high-frequency request patterns behind LB failover.

Repro steps (dev env):
1) Deploy control-plane change that performs alias swap followed by async fan-out invalidation.
2) Launch two edge nodes with staggered start and simulate request load with short TTL cached alias entries.
3) Trigger alias swap and verify that some requests to the node that sees invalidation first return 403 (race).
steps_to_mitigate:
Immediate mitigation applied:
- Reverted the non-atomic alias swap change at 2025-02-19 03:20 UTC (roll-back PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8123).
- Enabled emergency compatibility mode: edge cache check accepts either alias version for 60s while we stabilize propagation.
- Notified affected customers via Support (#SUP-12841, #SUP-12847) and applied per-tenant session refresh where needed.

Planned permanent fix:
1) Implement atomic alias swap using compare-and-swap with versioned binding writes and a propagation barrier so edge nodes will only invalidate caches after the authoritative write is durably acknowledged. (PR in flight: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8179).
2) Add a short-lived acceptance window on edges that tolerates two consecutive alias versions during upgrade windows to avoid 403 windows.
3) Add a control-plane monotonic epoch header to alias responses so edges can detect out-of-order updates and block until they can fetch the latest mapping.
4) Add e2e test in upgrade harness that simulates out-of-order delivery and asserts no 403s for valid API keys.

Rollout plan:
- Canary the atomic swap in dedicated-canary region (1 node pool) for 48 hours with telemetry flags enabled.
- Expand to remaining Dedicated regions in stages (24h per stage) if no regression.
- Private deploy customers: ship backported package to on-prem package repo; coordinate with Solutions for scheduled upgrade windows.

Monitoring / success metrics:
- Baseline 403 rate for apikey auth should be <0.01% across all Dedicated customers; target post-fix <0.001%.
- Add dashboards: "apikey-auth-403-by-epoch", propagation lag histogram, edge cache invalidation success rate.
- Alert if any tenant sees >0.1% 403 in a 5m window during rollout.
